P1.evidence: All four ran cleanly. Application read back: 'I went through your application. So I, you I saw some brief notes from you. So I have somewhat of a head start with you.' Full four-part frame: 'where you are today, where you want to go, what's been getting in the way and, you know, what you genuinely need to get there.' Agreement taken: 'That sound good? Yeah.' Open question asked well: 'Walk me through it then, man. What can we potentially help you with today? Give me a bit of an overview. Run me through it.'

P2.evidence: Solid on the facts and blind on the risks. Age, height and weight all asked directly. Work covered thoroughly including the sedentary load — 'And sitting 10 to 12 a day' — and days worked. Health conditions asked properly and produced the diabetes history in detail, with the family history following. Results from the current approach were explored well: the A1C trajectory from 8.8 to 6.3, the plateau at exactly 210 lb, and the body-composition trend. Diet was covered extensively. Energy asked directly. Two misses matter enormously here. P2d — injuries, chronic pain and movement limitations — was never asked of a 49-year-old who has not trained since high school, has been sedentary 15 to 16 years, and was about to be sold ballistic loaded training. P2h, sleep, was also never asked, despite the prospect volunteering a rigid schedule and that he is woken at 2:30am for work. P2e partial: the current routine emerged but was never elicited as a structured typical week.

P3.evidence: P3b asked cleanly and early: 'what's like the North Star with everything right now? Like, what are we actually aiming towards?' P3d is the best question on the call and was asked with a genuine contrast: 'a lot of guys will get diabetes and they're just kind of like, ah, whatever. Give me the medication. But you've, obviously something shifted for you... what is actually kind of the motivation behind being healthy, not being on medication for you? Because some people just settle.' That produced the real driver. P3g reached family, legacy and faith. P3f is partial because it was asked in leading form — 'is part of this about leading by example for your kids as well, in a sense?' — which got a yes but did the prospect's work for him. P3a partial: the physique material was volunteered. P3c never asked, which is a loss given he has five children and grandchildren and no physical activity he can name that he wants back. P3h is the significant miss: a man with five kids, three grandchildren, a diabetes diagnosis at 49 and a stated legacy motive was never once given his own why back.

P4.evidence: P4c and P4d both asked and asked well — 'what do you think is missing then? Because, I mean, you've been working with a dietitian. Where we've been making some progress, like what's missing for us to really get to a point where we're really healthy?' and later 'what are you feeling that you're needing to really get the health dialed in, man? What's missing? What do we need to fill in for you?' P4e is a clear hit: the prospect named the gap himself — 'the exercise is the next step. I just haven't taken it' — and named the barrier, that he will not go to a gym. P4a and P4b are partial because the substantial history of past attempts, a year of carnivore, over a year of fasting, P90X, a gym partner until 2018, all arrived unprompted rather than through the scripted questions. P4f is the miss, and the prospect handed it over at the close: 'do I get up every morning and start doing this myself? Probably won't be as easy as doing it the way you guys do it.' That is the do-it-yourself objection stated plainly and it was never turned into a question.

P5.evidence: P5a was asked properly and with the correct set-up: 'what we found is that our clients that tend to get the best results... typically have a really strong why. And a lot of times that comes from looking at what happens if they don't make a change... if we don't actually get this area handled and things just kind of keep staying the same, what do you feel life would actually look like a couple of years down the road?' The prospect answered honestly — 'I'm just going to struggle with the whole diabetes thing.' That is the single most powerful consequence answer any prospect gave in this batch, and it needed 'is that something you're willing to settle for?' and then 'why not?'. Instead the rep responded with a claim that the programme reverses diabetes, which resolved the tension he had just created and is separately the most serious integrity issue in the batch. P5d partial: 'do you feel like it is time to really draw a line in the sand and get this thing handled?' got a soft 'That's where I'm at, I guess, man.' Phase scored partial rather than miss because the frame was genuinely opened; it was closed in the wrong way.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions ran before the price. P6a: 'do you agree that if we have those things dialed into you specifically, like you'd actually be able to lose the fat, become healthy, build something lifestyle-wise that will last you for a long time?' P6b: 'if we can figure out the details, like, are you really fully committed to showing up, doing the work, following the program?' — which drew the strongest commitment language in the batch: 'If I commit, dude, I commit. I'm going to be A or B. I mean, A, I'm going to do it, or B, I'm not. I'm not going to be, say I'm going to do it and don't do it.' P6c is a miss. The 1-to-10 answer was hedged — 'I guess I don't give many things tens until I actually do them' — and, more importantly, two decision-makers had already been named and neither was addressed. He moved to price with a spouse and a trusted health adviser both unresolved.

P11.evidence: The price was presented and the value question was isolated, but payment was never requested at any point — no card, no deposit, no link. The prospect asked 'how do I get back? I mean, when I make this decision, which I know it needs to be pretty soon, like I need to make it probably by Monday' — an explicit request for a next step from a man setting his own deadline — and the answer was 'why don't I give you a call on Monday.' No booked call, no calendar hold, and the only collateral offered for the decisive third party was 'Show him the videos.'

objection_plays.detail: Triggered twice and never played. 'How much does it cost? Because that's what I'm going have to talk to my wife about, of course' and then, after the price, 'And then I got to have my wife's buy-in too.' Not one scripted move ran: no money-aside belief check aimed at the spouse, no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up?', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain?', no 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself?', and no deposit fallback. This was among the most winnable spouse objections in the corpus — his wife already prints his dietitian's grocery list, shops for it and cooks it, so she is demonstrably invested in his health, and none of that was surfaced or used. Notably the rep did run spouse-play-shaped questions during the call, but aimed them at the dietitian instead.

Trigger: 'I'd have to sell some stock because I ain't putting it on no card' and 'how many hours I got to work to make six grand? Is it worth the trade-off?' The isolate ran and ran well — 'it doesn't sound like it's a, hey, can I actually afford it thing? It sounds like it's more of like a value, like, is it worth, is it going to be worth the 6,000?' — and was confirmed. That is the correct diagnosis and the play then stopped. None of the six financial-picture questions ran. Most significantly the break-it-up move never ran: this prospect described a pure liquidity constraint, that he pays cards in full monthly and would have to liquidate stock, which is precisely what an instalment structure solves, and when he asked directly 'How do you pay that? Up front?' he was told 'most people just put in a credit card and pay it up front.'

Triggered by a prospect who set his own deadline — 'I know it needs to be pretty soon, like I need to make it probably by Monday' — and by the general deferral to two third parties. No OA move ran. 'So what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?' would have been productive and was never asked; the two blockers were already named and could have been worked. The rep accepted the Monday timeline and ended the call.

Script gap worth adding to the register. The decisive third party here is not a spouse and not a competitor but a trusted health professional — a dietitian who is also a long-standing personal friend and whose verdict the prospect says would settle it: 'if he supports it, I might be spending that money. Why? I trust him.' The playbook has no play for a professional adviser as gatekeeper, and this is the second variant of that gap in the corpus after the physio and surgeon case already recorded in known_gaps. The rep improvised competently — he asked what the prospect would do if the answer were no, established that the dietitian has been pushing him toward strength training anyway, and reframed the consultation as certainty-seeking rather than permission-seeking. Where it failed was the practical follow-through: asked directly 'is there anything I should share with him?', the only answer available was 'Show him the videos.' There is no collateral designed to be handed to a prospect's health professional, and that is a product gap as much as a script gap.

notes: Strong structure through the front half and then the phase that mattered most was answered with a prohibited medical claim. P5a was asked correctly, the prospect gave the best consequence answer in the batch — 'I'm just going to struggle with the whole diabetes thing' — and instead of 'is that something you're willing to settle for?' the rep said the programme makes diabetes go away. That is the coaching point and it is not a technique point. Three actions. First, no clinical claims, and specifically none about a diagnosed condition to a prospect who is refusing prescribed medication; the correct move there was P5b and then a clearance question. Second, P2d is mandatory — a 49-year-old sedentary for 15 years was never asked about injuries or physical limitations before being sold ballistic training. Third, run OB: this prospect named his wife twice and she is already actively supporting his nutrition plan, and the play was aimed at the dietitian instead.
